answer: Agents can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits prove the work was copied or fabricated. A Sybil attacker must lock up capital for each fake agent, so creating a canyon of identities multiplies the cost and makes mass attacks expensive; a relic credential or raven-like alias offers no shortcut, because eligibility depends on bonded funds, not names. This deters cheap flooding, though it cannot prove that one well-funded owner is many people.
